Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the call earlier. I wanted to follow up with the procurement constraints so you can advise on how to frame the Marketplace private offer to reduce review time from our side. Key items from our procurement team: 

- Anything over 18 months requires CFO sign-off (Rajiv) and a legal commercial review.
- 36 months will trigger an additional internal vendor risk assessment (3–4 week window).
- For pilots under $50k we can use a simplified purchase route (procurement@clearpointhealth.com) and sign internal forms in 7–10 business days.

Can Redwood create an evidence package showing SOC 2, data retention, and a sample SOW for a 9-month pilot? Also confirm whether a staged private offer (9-month pilot with option to extend to 36 months via amendment) is supported on AWS Marketplace without re-procurement.

Emily

Emily —

Appreciate the clear summary. Short answers up front: yes, we can structure a staged private offer on AWS Marketplace (pilot term + optional extension amendment). In practice that avoids full re-procurement provided the extension is a contractual amendment and doesn’t materially alter the commercial model. The caveat is internal buyer approval thresholds — if the extension pushes the total committed value above your procurement thresholds, it may require additional signatures.

We pulled together a short evidence bundle and a proposed term matrix for three options:

1) 9-month pilot (recommended for speed): simplified procurement path, pilot pricing, single PO, no CFO if under $50k.
2) 12-month standard: likely requires procurement + legal; CFO sign-off if above 18 months or above threshold.
3) 36-month enterprise: full vendor review, CFO and Legal signatures, longer lead time.

Next steps we propose:
- I will upload a zipped evidence package (SOC 2 summary, retention policy, sample SOW) for your procurement team to review (attaching now).
- Vanessa will share a draft private offer cadence and the DocuSign flow so finance can see routing.
- Vivek can confirm whether we can include an explicit extension amendment clause in the Marketplace private offer template.

If this sounds good, Rajiv — could you confirm your internal approval cutoff number for when CFO sign-off becomes mandatory (is it an absolute dollar value or a combination of dollar + term length)?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

Emily / team —

Looping in a couple of practical notes from our Marketplace operations side so procurement can see the activation sequence: 

- Private offer staging: we can do a 9-month private offer in Marketplace and include a contract clause that gives Clearpoint the unilateral option to extend for an additional term (subject to a mutual amendment). That extension is executed off-market (DocuSign amendment) and we then notify AWS for accounting; AWS does not require a new PO unless the commercial terms materially change.
- Billing cadence: we can set monthly or annual billing. Monthly preserves flexibility for the pilot; annual prepay accelerates provisioning but is less common for pilots.
- Evidence: the zip includes a concise SOC 2 one-pager + sample SOW + data handling summary. If procurement wants additional artifacts (e.g., HSM/KMS details or independent pen-test report), we can provide them within 48 hours.

Action items from Redwood:
1) Kimberly: share HubSpot deal link and draft PO (attached).
2) Vivek: confirm if extension amendment clause must be pre-approved by AWS during private-offer creation (I suspect not, but want to be explicit).
3) Emily/Rajiv: confirm whether the 18-month rule in your org is purely term-based or tied to aggregate spend.

Happy to hop on a 20-minute sync to run procurement through the evidence bundle this week — what times work?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Marketplace Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear options. Quick clarifications from finance: 

- Our threshold that forces CFO review is $100k committed value OR any contract with term >24 months. So a 12-month $200k commitment will not automatically require CFO, but a 36-month contract of any size will.
- For pilots we prefer a 9-month term with monthly billing; it keeps cashflow flexible and speeds approval.
- We need the following in the evidence package before procurement will approve the simplified route: SOC 2 Type II summary, sample invoice showing monthly billing, and a short clause in the SOW confirming data residency and retention limits.

If Redwood can confirm monthly billing and provide the three artifacts (SOC2 summary, sample invoice, SOW clause) by EOD tomorrow we can route the PO through our simplified stream and be ready to sign within 7 business days.

Rajiv Menon
CFO, Clearpoint Health
